text: Susan Victoria Lucci, born December 23, 1946, in Scarsdale, New York, is an American actress best known for portraying Erica Kane on the ABC daytime drama All My Children from January 16, 1970, to September 23, 2011, during the show's entire network run. The character is considered an icon in American soap opera history and is regarded as the most popular character in the genre; TV Guide has called her "unequivocally the most famous soap opera character in the history of daytime TV" and included her in their 2013 list of The 60 Nastiest Villains of All Time. Lucci was nominated 21 times for the Daytime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series, winning once in 1999 after the 19th nomination, with her status as a perpetual nominee drawing significant media attention since the late 1980s. Her image became widely recognized as synonymous with never winning an Emmy, a phenomenon highlighted by NBC's Saturday Night Live, which featured her hosting an episode with cast and crew using Emmys as props, and a 1989 Sweet One commercial in which she shouted, "Eleven years without an Emmy! What does a person have to do around here to get an Emmy?" After 18 nominations, she won the award in 1999, receiving a standing ovation presented by Shemar Moore. She was named one of VH1's 200 Top Icons of All Time and one of Barbara Walters's Ten Most Fascinating People. Lucci graduated from Garden City High School in 1964 and Marymount College, Tarrytown, in 1968 with a BA in drama. She began her television career with bit parts on Love Is a Many Splendored Thing and The Doctors, and had uncredited roles in the 1969 films Goodbye, Columbus and Me, Natalie. She also appeared in a 1982 cameo in Young Doctors in Love, guest-starred in prime time series such as The Love Boat, Fantasy Island, and The Fall Guy, and played leading roles in films including Invitation to Hell (1984), Anastasia: The Mystery of Anna (1986), Mafia Princess (1986), Haunted by Her Past (1985), Lady Mobster (1988), and The Bride in Black (1990). In 1995, she starred as Elizabeth 'Ebbie' Scrooge in the Lifetime film Ebbie, a Christmas Carol update, which received positive reviews. In 1999, she played Annie Oakley in the revival of Annie Get Your Gun. She guest-starred in episodes of Hope & Faith (2004), That's So Raven (2005), and appeared in the 2015 film Joy. From 2010 to 2014, she made multiple appearances on Hot in Cleveland as herself, including the episode "Life with Lucci," and appeared in Gloria Estefan's music video "Hotel Nacional" in February 2012. She guest-starred in multi-episodes of Army Wives in 2012 and hosted and narrated the 2012–2014 Investigation Discovery series Deadly Affairs. In 2013, she began starring as Geneviève Delatour in the Lifetime series Devious Maids, which ran until 2016, and her comedic performance was well received. In 2017, she appeared in Sia's music video "Santa's Coming for Us" and guest-starred in an episode of Difficult People, as well as in Progressive Insurance television ads styled as soap operas. In 2023, she received a Lifetime Achievement Award at the 50th Daytime Emmy Awards. In 2024, after a seven-year acting hiatus, she returned to film in the black comedy Outcome, starring alongside Keanu Reeves, Jonah Hill, and Cameron Diaz. Lucci married Helmut Huber on September 13, 1969; they have two children, actress Liza Huber and son Andreas Huber, and were married for 52 years until his death on March 28, 2022, at age 84. She is a registered Republican and has hosted fundraising events for Rudy Giuliani, and is a supporter of LGBT rights, inspired by a 2000 All My Children storyline in which her character Erica's daughter, Bianca Montgomery, came out as a lesbian. In late 2018, she underwent an emergency procedure to place two arterial stents in her heart due to blocked arteries, and postponed publicizing the event until shortly before the American Heart Association's Go Red for Women event in February 2019. Lucci also owns The Susan Lucci Collection, a line of hair care, perfumes, lingerie, and skin care products.
